incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected for model-serving runtime (service: model-runner-prod). error-rate spike 12:35-12:45 UTC. paging @sam oncall.

Jess: got the page — I'm on it. seeing 5xx spikes from model-runner across 3 availability zones. first glance looks like OOM / segfault in the quantized kernel.

Sam: confirm which model and build? any rollouts recently?

Jess: traffic concentrated on model redwood-llama-70b-q8b:v3 (quantized kernel q8b). no config rollouts in last 2 hours. we did push a kernel opt earlier this week but it was staged.

leo: uploading a quick log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T12:37:11Z] runner[pid=4521] ERROR kernel_q8b.cpp: allocation failed: requested 14.2G, available 9.6G -> SIGSEGV
[2026-03-15T12:37:11Z] runner[pid=4521] FATAL unwind: double free at 0x7fe8...
[2026-03-15T12:37:11Z] gateway 5xx_count +1 route=/v1/generate model=redwood-llama-70b-q8b
```

Jess: error-rate by minute: 5xx went from baseline 0.4% -> 18% at peak. impacted p95 latency for same window spiked from 210ms -> 1.2s.

maria: customers reported: CS has three active customers showing increased errors: cust-42 (chatbot), cust-112 (search ranking), cust-7 (analytics). CS: cust-42 seeing 35% of calls failing.

cs-team: acknowledged, we notified cust-42 and cust-112 that we're investigating and provided temporary mitigation guidance (fallback to smaller model).

Sam: immediate mitigation plan: 1) split traffic away from q8b model to fallback q4f smaller model for 40% of production queries 2) disable batching on q8b runners for long sequences 3) restart affected model-runner pods one AZ at a time 4) enable kernel backoff flag to force memory-conservative path. any issues?

Jess: implementing step 1 now — creating a routing policy to route 40% to redwood-llama-70b-q4f:v2 and 60% to original. will roll out in 5% increments.

ops-bot: action started: traffic-split job kicked (job-id: ts-2150006789-split).

Leo: while traffic split is rolling, I'll patch runner config to disable large continuous batching (max_batch_tokens=4096 -> 1024) and set QUANT_HEAP_LIMIT=12G on the quant kernel. patch applied on node set a.

Jess: confirming: after first 10% shift error-rate dropped to 9%. after 30% shift down to 4.6%. good sign.

Sam: schedule rolling restarts for remaining affected pods in AZ-b and AZ-c. do a canary restart first.

Jess: canary restart done on runner-az-b-03; canary booted clean, no segfaults in logs, p95 latency stable. proceeding with remainder.

maria: ETA for full mitigation? CS asked for an ETA to tell customers.

Jess: full traffic split to 40% fallback + batching reduction + restarts should be complete in ~18 minutes. will update at 12:58 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigation in progress — customer impact reduced. current 5xx rate: 2.8% (12:50 UTC).

Sam: root-cause hypothesis: quantized kernel path for q8b under long-sequence + higher batch memory pressure triggers allocation beyond heap -> oom -> segfault. regression likely from upstream kernel optimization earlier this week.

Leo: capturing commands used for quick triage: 
```bash
# show top OOM/segfault logs
journalctl -u model-runner -S "2026-03-15T12:30:00" | grep -E "ERROR|FATAL|SIGSEGV" -n
# bump QUANT_HEAP_LIMIT env on deployment
kubectl set env deployment/model-runner QUANT_HEAP_LIMIT=12G -n prod
# patch config to lower batch tokens
kubectl patch cm model-runner-config -n prod --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_batch_tokens":"1024"}}'
```

Jess: post-mitigation next steps: 1) revert routing once kernel fix is validated OR keep fallback for 24-48h if stable, 2) collect heap profiles from affected nodes, 3) engage runtime team to audit q8b kernel changes and add repro harness for long-seq cases.

maria: I'm taking over the on-call at 13:00 UTC — will do a 10-minute handoff summary and own the postmortem. @sam handing off.

Sam: handing off to @maria. current state: mitigations applied, 5xx down to 1.1%, routing split 40% to fallback, batch tokens lowered, restarts completed. will follow up on kernel PR review.

maria: received. I'll keep pages if regressions or timeouts pop up. scheduling postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC. tagging runtime and ml-infra.

ops-bot: note: one node in AZ-c showed high GPU memory fragmentation; flagged for deeper analysis (ticket INF-5421).

Leo: quick note for postmortem data: please save these artifacts: heap profiles, allocator traces, model-runner core dumps, routing config at time of incident.

Jess: collecting cores and uploading to s3://redwood-incidents/2150006789/cores.tar.gz. starting profiler dump job.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) at 12:57 UTC — operators to monitor for 2 hours; owner: maria.

maria: closing notes: customer impact contained via routing fallback. follow-up: runtime to revert risky kernel optimization or add safety checks; CS to follow up with cust-42 and cust-112 tomorrow. I'll own postmortem doc and assign owners. :white_check_mark:
